text: A count of 14 and a count of 19 could mean several different things. Mara pulls both raw account lists and does the only thing that actually answers the question: a direct, account-by-account set comparison.
The method is a standard set reconciliation: which accounts appear in both lists, which are only in the audit's list, and which are only in the automation's list.
The result is clean. All 14 audit accounts are also in the automation's list. Zero accounts are only in the audit's list. Exactly 5 accounts are only in the automation's list.

This rules out a data error on either side -- the automation's 19 is a strict superset of the audit's 14. What remains is a precise question: who are these 5 accounts, and how did they get this access.
